title: Exponent-loading execution
statement: Let $E,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathcal{O}$ be a Boolean-valued function on four indices and finite Boolean words, and let $x$ be a finite Boolean word. Suppose $k,j\in\mathbb{N}$, $j<E+1$, $j+k=E$, and $\mathrm{st}$ is a state with $\mathrm{st}.X=j$, every register at most $B$, $E\le B$, and $\mathrm{st}.P+1\le B$. Then the program $A_E$ has a finite run from the configuration with label $\mathrm{ld}(j)$, registers $\mathrm{st}$, and no answer to the configuration with label $\mathrm{pw}$, $X=E$, $P=\mathrm{st}.P+1$, every other register unchanged, and no answer. Every configuration strictly before the final one satisfies the guard for $A_E$, input $x$, and bound $B$.
hypotheses_covered: An oracle assigning a Boolean to each of four indices and finite Boolean words
Every register of $\mathrm{st}$ is at most $B$
replaced:
Let $E,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathcal{O}$ be an oracle on four indices and bit strings,
and let $x$ be a bit string. For all $k,j\in\mathbb{N}$ and register states
$\mathrm{st}$, suppose $j<E+1$, $j+k=E$, $\mathrm{st}.X=j$, every register of
$\mathrm{st}$ is at most $B$, $E\le B$, and $\mathrm{st}.P+1\le B$. Then there is a
finite run, guarded by bound $B$ before its final configuration, from label
$\mathrm{ld}(j)$ with registers $\mathrm{st}$ and no answer to label $\mathrm{pw}$ with
$X=E$, $P=\mathrm{st}.P+1$, all other registers unchanged, and no answer.
